title: Unsupervised learning and probabilistic models
stage: College AI and machine learning degree
audience: a college student in an artificial intelligence, machine learning or computer science degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Find structure in unlabeled data: k-means and its initialization, hierarchical and density-based clustering, Gaussian mixture models and the EM algorithm, principal component analysis by the SVD, low-dimensional embeddings, matrix factorization for recommender systems, anomaly detection, hidden Markov models with the forward and Viterbi algorithms, and an introduction to probabilistic graphical models.
primary_reading: Probabilistic Machine Learning: An Introduction by Kevin Murphy (free PDF)

weeks.5: Principal component analysis and the SVD
weeks.6: Embeddings for visualization: MDS, t-SNE and UMAP
weeks.9: Hidden Markov models and the forward algorithm
weeks.11: Probabilistic graphical models: Bayesian networks and Markov random fields

blocks.deliverable: Cluster a small data set three ways and compare the results.
Run two iterations of EM by hand on a one-dimensional mixture.
Compute the principal components of a small data set.
Week 7 midterm; factorize a small ratings matrix by alternating least squares.
Decode the most likely hidden state sequence for a small HMM.
Answer a query in a small Bayesian network by enumeration.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Segmentation and anomaly report: on a supplied unlabeled data set, standardize the features, run k-means and a Gaussian mixture model, choose the number of clusters with a stated criterion, project the data with PCA, flag anomalies, and write a report that interprets each cluster and states what the methods cannot tell you.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
